C7.comment: For numeric FAC, convert/check the byte, then allocate a one-character string in FAC on success
C7.evidence: $08B4 selects $1E9E; $17BB checks the converted high byte; the low byte is staged at $0100 for the length-one $1D6E allocation.  Normal completion jumps to $0926 without fetching an inline operand.

EE.comment: Load integer ARG from two bytes at ${value:04X}, high byte first
EE.evidence: $0902 selects $2054.  With binary arithmetic, $21A6 reads the little-endian address at IP+1 and IP+2, leaves IP advanced by two, and returns Y=0.  The handler sets $B6=1 and reads offsets 0 and 1 into $6C and $6D, then jumps to $0926 for the final increment.

F1.comment: Load integer FAC from two bytes at ${value:04X}, high byte first
F1.evidence: $0908 selects $2042.  Its $21A6 helper fetches the address low then high at IP+1 and IP+2, advancing the cursor by two.  $1FEB sets $B5=1, reads offsets 0 and 1 into $64 and $65 respectively, then jumps to $0926 for the final increment.

F4.comment: Store numeric FAC as a two-byte word at ${value:04X}, high byte first, on normal completion
F4.evidence: $090E selects $20A8: fetch destination low at IP+1 and high at IP+2; with $B5 zero call $BC1B then $B1AA.  Store $64 then $65 via ($3D),Y and jump to $0926 for the final cursor increment.
